questions.q: The coefficient of $x^n$ in the expansion of $\frac{e^{7 x}+e^x}{e^{3 x}}$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{e^{7 x}+e^x}{e^{3 x}} \Rightarrow e^{4 x}+e^{-2 x}$
Series of $e^a=1+\frac{a}{1!}+\frac{a^2}{2!}+\frac{a^3}{3!} \ldots\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow e^{4 x}+ & e^{-2 x}=\left(1+\frac{4 x}{1!}+\frac{(4 x)^2}{2!}+\frac{(4 x)^3}{3!}+\ldots\right) \\
& +\left(1+\frac{(-2 x)}{1!}+\frac{(-2 x)^2}{2!}+\ldots \ldots\right)
\end{aligned}$
Here, coefficient of
$\begin{aligned}
& x^2 \equiv \frac{4^2}{2!}+\frac{(-2)^2}{2!} \\
& x^3  \equiv \frac{4^3}{3!}+\frac{(-2)^3}{3!} \\
& \vdots \\
& x^n=\frac{4^n}{n!}+\frac{(-2)^n}{n!}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $x^{18}$ occurs in the rth term in the expansion of $\left(x^4+\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}$, then what is the value of $r$ ?
questions.solution:
In the expansion of $\left(x^4+\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}$, let $T_r$ is the $r^{\text {th }}$ term
$\begin{aligned} \\ T_r & =\binom{15}{r-1}\left(x^4\right)^{15-r+1}\left(\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{r-1} \\ \\ & =\binom{15}{r-1} x^{64-4 r-3 r+3}=15_{C_{r-1}} x^{67-7 r} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{x}^{18}$ occurs in this term
$\Rightarrow 18=67-7 r \Rightarrow 7 r=49 \Rightarrow r=7 .$

From the given condition, replacing $a$ by a and $-a i$ respectively, we get

which is divisible by \(x^2+x+1\).

questions.solution:
The two letters, the first and the last of the four lettered word can be chosen in \((17)^2\) ways, as repetition is allowed for consonants. The two vowels in the middle are distinct so that the number of ways of filling up the two places is \({ }^5 \mathrm{P}_2=20\).

questions.q: The general solution of \(8 \tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}=1+\sec x\) is
questions.solution:
We have, \(8 \tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}=1+\sec x\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 8\left(\frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x}\right)=1+\frac{1}{\cos x}=\frac{1+\cos x}{\cos x} \\
& \Rightarrow 8 \cos x-8 \cos ^2 x=(1+\cos x)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow 9 \cos ^2 \mathrm{x}-6 \cos \mathrm{x}+1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(3 \cos \mathrm{x}-1)^2=0 \Rightarrow 3 \cos \mathrm{x}-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos \mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{3}=\cos \alpha \text { (say) }  \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2 \mathrm{n} \pi \pm \alpha \\
& \therefore \mathrm{x}=2 \mathrm{n} \pi \pm \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \text { where } \mathrm{n} \in \mathrm{I}
\end{aligned}\)
